label: copy-phase, weakly selective for outputting g or v
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps). About 95% of activation mass falls in the copy phase, concentrated on recall_idx 1-4 and almost never during the original phase (none at t=0,1). Within the copy phase it prefers steps whose output is g (14.7x lift) or v (11.1x), with weaker lifts for input g and next_out v/s. The largest activations come on sequences with g/v runs (e.g. g v v x, s g g g v), reading g or emitting g. Still, the best simple predicate (copy phase and out_tok in {g,v}) has only about 15% precision and covers about half the mass. Most outputs of g/v do not fire it, and about half the mass lands on other tokens with no clear pattern. Adding next_out, in_tok or position conditions did not help: dev F1 stayed at or below 0.23. Magnitude is higher on g/v-heavy sequences, but I could not find a clean rule for it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: g, v, 3, l, s, j; least: d, c, f, 0) and the next token to output (most: v, s, x, t, 3, g; least: o, d, c, 0); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=4.
